name: IN-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a +15 Republican lean
Incumbent Erin Houchin running with a large financial advantage
model.rationale: The district's +15 Republican lean, Houchin's incumbency and roughly 18-to-1 fundraising edge, and markets pricing her at 94% all point to a comfortable Republican win with no evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or polling showing Meyer within single digits would warrant a relook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Erin Houchin seeks a third term in a southern Indiana district that leans about 15 points Republican. She has raised more than $1.8 million and holds over $1.1 million on hand, while Democratic nominee Brad Meyer has raised about $105,000 with modest cash remaining. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but has minimal funding.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Houchin roughly a 94% chance of winning. The fundamentals, money gap, and market pricing all align on a decisive Republican victory, with the only real question being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
